judge_output.rationale: Barmby et al. 2012 (2012AJ....143...87B) already compared integrated 3.6 and 4.5 um (IRAC) colours of massive old M31 globular clusters with simple-stellar-population predictions. They found the models reproduce the colours reasonably well, apart from a small, not statistically significant red offset in [4.5]-[5.8] attributed to missing circumstellar dust. That is a closely related test of an integrated 3-5 um excess over SSP models, run on broadband photometry with a smaller, M31-only sample. The card's SPHEREx spectral version adds the Milky Way clusters, a per-cluster outlier fraction above 5 per cent, CO-band modelling and a radial-profile test. The Ĝ survey (2014ApJ...792...27W, 2015ApJS..217...25G) sets waste-heat limits on whole galaxies, not on globular clusters.

closest_prior.relation: Tested integrated IRAC 3.6/4.5/5.8 um colours of massive M31 globular clusters against SSP models and found agreement except a small, insignificant [4.5]-[5.8] red offset; it used Spitzer photometry of a smaller M31-only sample, with no per-cluster outlier census or waste-heat framing.
Formalism converting mid-IR excess into waste-heat luminosity limits, applied to galaxies rather than globular clusters.
WISE search of ~1e5 galaxies for mid-IR reprocessing of starlight, giving upper limits at galaxy scale with no cluster-level SSP-residual analysis.
Found up to 0.2 mag V-K offsets between M31 globular cluster colours and SSP models, attributed to model systematics; this covers only the optical-near-IR, not 3-5 um.

judge_output.what_would_make_it_open: No listed work delivers a per-cluster SPHEREx spectral census of the 3.5-5 um excess over SSP fits to 0.75-2.5 um for both Milky Way and M31 globular clusters, with an outlier fraction above 5 per cent, tests against metallicity and AGB counts, and radial-profile checks.
